records.summary: A desktop setup and recovery tool for Linux with tested configuration presets, diagnostics, and rollback. It would help users configure a desktop environment and restore its settings.
records.paid_demand: The report records 2 paying-proof snippets, but does not identify what was paid for or provide verified revenue.

competitors.name: Save Desktop
competitors.note: Backs up, restores, and synchronizes configurations across Linux desktop environments.

competitors.name: Kubuntu
competitors.note: Maintained desktop flavor; free platform alternative.

competitors.name: Lubuntu
competitors.note: Maintained desktop flavor; free platform alternative.

rounds.plain: K0 means the core setup and recovery workflow looks quick to copy, and Save Desktop already covers configuration recovery. K2 is met by at least two competing launches; K3 by platform maintainers shipping desktop environments; K4 by more than five free desktop options without a demonstrated wedge. K1 thresholds are unverified, and recent releases do not show that demand is gone.

risks: The complaint examples mix performance, visual layout, and virtualization issues.
Automation and founder-hours thresholds are unverified.
A distinct product wedge is unverified.
records.moat: The report finds no defensible moat: presets and configuration recovery are readily reproducible, and Save Desktop already covers the core workflow.
